extracted.intended_audience: R package authors, prospective reviewers, and the scientific software community
extracted.subtask_description: Description of rOpenSci's onboarding peer code review process for R packages, including how packages are evaluated, how reviews are conducted (via GitHub), lessons learned, and ideas for scaling and improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: When an author submits a package, our editors evaluate it for fit according to our criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may turn packages away prior to review when they are out-of-scope. Because submitted packages are already public and open-source, rOpenSci does not emphasize 'time to publication' and generally does not explicitly reject packages except for lack of fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the package for usability based on rOpenSci guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usability is assessed alongside quality and style; rOpenSci provides reviewer guidance (including links to previous reviews) to help reviewers judge usability. The public issue thread allows discussion between reviewers and authors about usability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the package for quality based on rOpenSci guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality encompasses finding bugs, ensuring code can be installed and run across systems (complementing CRAN checks), tests, and adherence to best practices. Reviewers may recommend CI, tests, and other quality-improving changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the package for coding style and general software style based on rOpenSci guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style assessments aim to promote best practices and maintainability. The process includes guidance for reviewers and examples in previous reviews to illustrate desired style standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open, public GitHub-based review process
rubrics_metrics.description: The system works entirely through the GitHub issue system; reviewers post reviews as comments on that issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes the entire process open and public from the start, with reviewers and authors known to each other and free to communicate directly. Public review incentivizes good behavior and transparency and enables others to learn from the discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-adversarial focus
rubrics_metrics.description: A design goal is to keep reviews non-adversarial — to focus on improving software quality rather than judging the package or authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Openness of the process and adherence to a code of conduct are intended to encourage civil, constructive reviews. Reviews should aim to help authors improve their packages rather than to attack them.

rubrics_metrics.name: No explicit rejection policy (hold-to-revise model)
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci does not generally explicitly reject packages; packages requiring significant revisions can remain on hold until authors incorporate changes and update the discussion thread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy reflects that packages are already public; however, it can create ambiguity about process endpoints and reviewer motivation if authors do not follow up — rOpenSci considers enforcing deadlines for author responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer direct contributions (pull requests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers can contribute to the package directly via a pull request when this is more efficient than describing the changes they suggest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing direct contributions accelerates fixes and reduces friction; submitting changes as PRs leverages GitHub workflows and can improve the efficiency of implementing reviewer suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of GitHub features for collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers can publicly consult others by @tagging if outside expertise is wanted and can use in-line commenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leveraging GitHub's collaborative features (tagging, inline comments, PRs) supports efficient review, invites outside expertise, and provides a record of the conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous integration and automated testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage the use of continuous integration (CI) and testing as part of package quality standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many reviewers and reviewees learned the value of CI. rOpenSci may add rOpenSci-specific tests and move some setup burden from authors to an automated pipeline. CI helps ensure cross-system installation and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear communication of process start and end
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about how to get started with a review and how the review is supposed to wrap up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: rOpenSci updated its reviewer guide and added links to previous reviews to clarify the beginning. For the end, because there are no rejections, it's important to define expectations (e.g., deadlines for author response) so reviewers know when a review is effectively closed or stalled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manageable reviewer time commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and limit the time burden on reviewers; reported review times ranged from 1–10 hours (average ~4 hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reviewing is volunteer work, the process should aim to limit the burden (e.g., via automation, better guidance, distributing work across editors/reviewers). Time estimates are useful to set expectations for prospective reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling and reviewer incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop mechanisms to build an experienced reviewer base, maintain enthusiasm, and avoid overburdening reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideas include expanding the reviewer pool via networks, using multiple 'handling editors' to assign and track reviews, and providing incentives or recognition to sustain volunteer effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author incentives and credit mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Find ways to help package authors gain greater visibility and credit after packages pass review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential incentives include badges (e.g., Center for Open Science, Mozilla Science Lab) or easier routes to publishing software papers to attract more authors to participate in the extra work required by review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automation to reduce manual burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Automate parts of the review process to increase value for reviewer and reviewee time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions include submitting packages as pull requests to better use GitHub features, creating automated pipelines to set up CI and tests for authors, and using automated reminders to keep reviewers and editors on schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote learning and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the review process to drive adoption of best practices among authors and reviewers (e.g., CI, documentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey responses indicated that many participants learned new practices and valued learning from reviews; the process should highlight and teach best practices as part of the review feedback.
